players.product: Helios AI/HPC data-center campus (West Texas, 800 gross MW) leased to CoreWeave, plus Merlin / Caspian / Selene Texas development sites - ex-Bitcoin-mining site (Galaxy Power)

quarterly_data.signal: In Q2, Phase I of our Helios data center came online with the first 133 MW of critical IT delivered to CoreWeave. We delivered Phase I at Helios on schedule and on budget; all data halls delivered to CoreWeave under the Phase I lease agreement prior to quarter end. The campus is now generating cash flow.
quarterly_data.figure: 133 MW critical IT delivered to CoreWeave (Phase I), on schedule and on budget

capex.display: 133 MW critical IT delivered (Helios Phase I)

quarterly_data.signal: With Phase I now fully online, beginning in the third quarter, we expect Phase I to generate its first full quarter of leasing revenue of approximately $80 million and a project-level adjusted EBITDA margin of over 90%.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$80M Phase I leasing revenue per quarter from Q3 2026; >90% project-level adjusted EBITDA margin

quarterly_data.signal: Data center CapEx was $448 million in Q2, up from $354 million in Q1. In the coming quarters, you should expect CapEx to continue increasing alongside the pace of construction at Helios. We also recognized a clean electricity investment tax credit of approximately $65 million. The Data Centers Segment had approximately $2.5 billion in total assets and $1.5 billion in total liabilities.
quarterly_data.figure: Data-center capex $448M in Q2 (vs $354M Q1), rising

quarterly_data.signal: On July 28th, we completed a private 144A offering of $3.5 billion of five-year senior secured notes structured at an 85% loan to cost - the largest financing in our history. Combined with the equity Galaxy has already contributed, this funds the remainder of Phase II at Helios, which will add an additional 260 MW of critical IT capacity starting next year. Phase II is now 100% funded from a debt and equity perspective; the equity expected for Phase III is already pre-funded.
quarterly_data.figure: $3.5B five-year senior secured notes at 85% loan-to-cost; Phase II = 260 MW critical IT, fully funded

quarterly_data.signal: Phase II: HITT Contracting joined as our new general contractor (replacing Clayco, Phase I GC) and has been mobilized on site since April; earthwork complete, structural foundation work underway. We expect to commence Phase II data hall deliveries in the second quarter of 2027. Phase II comprises eight data halls in total, with seven online by the end of 2027, and the final data hall following in early 2028. The third and final phase of Helios one, an additional 200 MW of gross power and 133 MW of critical IT load, is expected to come online throughout 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: Phase II deliveries from Q2 2027 (7 of 8 halls by end-2027); Phase III 133 MW critical IT through 2028

quarterly_data.signal: On our remaining 830 MW of approved capacity at Helios Two (energization slated for late 2028), conversations continue to advance across hyperscalers, Neoclouds, some of the labs themselves, and some new entrants; new guarantee and lease wrap structures are being formalized. We've already placed deposits and issued purchase orders on more than $180 million of long-lead electrical equipment, including main power transformers and switchgear. West's Pitchfork switching station is under construction to support energization of this 830 MW.
quarterly_data.figure: 830 MW approved at Helios Two unleased, late-2028 energization; >$180M long-lead electrical equipment ordered

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline: beyond the existing 1.6 GW of approved capacity across Helios one and two, incremental expansion of two gigawatts split across Helios three and Helios four (Helios three: 1 GW submitted for Batch Zero with $50 million of financial security posted). Three new Texas sites: Merlin (500 acres McGregor Industrial Park, initial 74 MW phase energizing 2028, path to 500 MW), Caspian (700 MW, Batch Zero base load eligible) and Selene (900 MW, Batch Zero study load, $45 million security posted). Helios and our three new campuses bring our total potential power capacity to more than 5.7 GW.
quarterly_data.figure: >5.7 GW total potential power capacity; 1.6 GW approved at Helios; Caspian 700 MW base-load eligible

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers generated $20 million of adjusted gross profit and $11 million of adjusted EBITDA in Q2, both reflecting the phased delivery of data halls throughout the quarter. Total data center operating expenses, excluding pass-through operator costs, were $21 million. Firm-wide: GAAP net loss of $85 million, adjusted EBITDA of negative $77 million driven by digital asset price depreciation; 72% of equity capital now allocated to the two operating businesses.
quarterly_data.figure: Data-center segment adjusted gross profit $20M, adjusted EBITDA $11M (first operating quarter)

quarterly_data.signal: Governor Abbott directed the PUCT and ERCOT to conduct a comprehensive audit of all data center projects seeking grid interconnection; we no longer expect communication on Batch Zero classification in the coming days. Forward market demand for power and compute is stronger today than it's ever been, while forward market supply of new projects is very quickly being constrained by both physical delivery and political headwinds. Leases for power at this scale are increasingly being signed well ahead of energization.

Leasing revenue reflects total contracted rent over the life of each lease, including annual escalators, recognized straight-line; power and utility charges are passed through to the customer.
